input: Organize a clothing drive for the local shelter

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what types and sizes of clothing are needed prevents collecting unusable donations and focuses the drive on what the shelter actually needs.
Whether this is a solo effort or involves a team, school, workplace, or community group completely changes the coordination, communication, and delegation plan.
The physical location for drop-off collection points and the setting (office, neighborhood, school) determines outreach strategy and logistics.
A hard deadline for when donations must be delivered to the shelter is the central scheduling constraint that drives the entire timeline.
Budget availability for supplies like bins, flyers, or bags determines what promotional and collection materials can be used.
Whether the drive is publicized broadly or kept within a specific group affects outreach tone, channels used, and expected volume of donations.
Understanding how donations will physically get to the shelter — self-drop-off, scheduled pickup, or volunteer transport — determines end-stage planning.

gold.taskTitle: Organize a clothing drive for the local shelter
gold.taskDescription: Plan and execute a clothing donation drive to collect and deliver clothing items to a local shelter.

questions.title: What clothing types or sizes does the shelter specifically need?
questions.description: Determine whether the shelter has a stated need for specific items such as winter coats, children's clothing, men's or women's sizes, or undergarments, so the drive can be targeted accordingly.

questions.title: Who is helping you run this drive?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a solo effort or involves a group such as coworkers, classmates, neighbors, or a community organization, to shape the coordination and delegation plan.

questions.title: Where will you set up donation collection points?
questions.description: Identify the physical locations where donation bins or drop-off spots will be placed, such as a workplace, school, apartment building, or public space.

questions.title: What is your deadline for delivering donations to the shelter?
questions.description: Establish the hard end date by which all collected clothing must reach the shelter, which will anchor the entire drive timeline.

questions.title: Do you have a budget for supplies like bins or flyers?
questions.description: Determine whether there is money available for collection materials, printed promotional content, bags, or other supplies, or if the drive must rely entirely on free or donated resources.

questions.title: How widely do you want to publicize the drive?
questions.description: Decide whether outreach should be broad and community-facing via social media and public postings, or limited to a specific internal group such as an office or school.

questions.title: How will collected clothing be transported to the shelter?
questions.description: Determine the delivery method — such as volunteer drivers, a rented vehicle, scheduled shelter pickup, or personal drop-off — to plan the final logistics step.
